summary: Acme Retail — transient KV cache eviction causing partial completions and billing exposure (post-incident follow-up)
description: Issue summary: Between 2026-03-05 04:12 UTC and 2026-03-05 04:46 UTC Acme Retail saw a spike of truncated / partial completions for chat and completion endpoints. Impact: users observed missing tails in generated responses and higher-than-expected token billing for repeated retries. Environment: production, dedicated GPU pool (acme-dedicated-us-east), model variants: gptx-13b-quant and gptx-13b-std. This ticket captures the post-incident investigation, mitigation, customer communication, and action plan.
impact: ~12% of Acme's requests in the 34-minute window returned incomplete final chunks (stream closed early) leading to increased client retries and a billing delta estimate of +$1,200 for the window. Customer reported degraded storefront personalization for ~30 minutes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use Acme's traffic pattern: many short-prefix requests with unique conversation IDs (high cardinality KV entries).
2) Inject a transient downscale on serving nodes (simulate GPU pool transient reclamation).
3) Observe KV cache eviction logs and subsequent partial completions for in-flight streaming requests.
4) Repeat with quantized variant (gptx-13b-quant) to surface tokenization boundary mismatches.
logs: svc-serving-runtime:evict:2026-03-05T04:23:18Z - evicted 1,283 KV entries due to memory_pressure_high
svc-streaming:session:2026-03-05T04:24:01Z - session 0x7f8e closed mid-stream (client reported partial chunk)
autoscaler:decision:2026-03-05T04:22:45Z - downscale triggered to reclaim GPUs (reason: transient host preempt)
investigation_notes: Initial triage (Support): correlated customer complain timestamps with autoscaler events and serving runtime eviction metrics.
SRE hypothesis: autoscaler downscale combined with aggressive KV eviction policy caused in-flight KV contexts to be removed, resulting in stream resumptions seeing missing KV state and closing early.

Edge case: quantized model variant uses different tokenization/chunking heuristic; when KV entries are evicted mid-session the runtime attempted a fallback that truncated remaining tokens instead of transparent rebuffering.
Reproduced locally by running high-cardinality prefix workload against a downscaled node set; observed identical partial-completion behavior and same log signatures.
Found telemetry gap: session-level correlation ID was not being written to the eviction trace for quantized variants (makes post-hoc recon easier).
workaround: Short-term: enabled conservative KV retention for Acme's dedicated pool (increased retention by 3x) and disabled automatic downscale for 60 minutes during peak hours. Customers instructed to retry with idempotent client logic (server returned 499 for aborted streams).
resolution: Deployed hotfix (serving-runtime v2.4.7) that: 1) makes eviction preemption-aware for in-flight sessions, 2) adds transparent rebuffer path for quantized variants, and 3) writes session correlation metadata to eviction traces. Patch was rolled out to Acme's dedicated pool with canary -> full rollout completed by 2026-03-07 18:00 UTC. Customer was issued a billing credit for the exposure window.
